You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0235.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

args.command:
cat > build.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem,rdMolDescriptors
from rdkit.Geometry import Point3D
import numpy as np
names=['a','b','c','d','e','f','g','h','i','j','k','l','m','n','q','r','N','Me','Op','Ob','Oa']
elems=['C']*16+['N','C','O','O','O']
rw=Chem.RWMol()
for i,el in enumerate(elems):
    at=Chem.Atom(el)
    if i<6: at.SetIsAromatic(True)
    rw.AddAtom(at)
for x,y in [('a','b'),('b','c'),('c','d'),('d','e'),('e','f'),('f','a')]: rw.AddBond(names.index(x),names.index(y),Chem.BondType.AROMATIC)
for x,y in [('c','g'),('g','h'),('h','i'),('i','j'),('j','d'),('i','k'),('l','m'),('m','n'),('n','j'),('j','q'),('q','r'),('r','N'),('N','h'),('N','Me'),('f','Op'),('e','Ob'),('Ob','n'),('m','Oa')]: rw.AddBond(names.index(x),names.index(y),Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
rw.AddBond(10,11,Chem.BondType.DOUBLE)
mol=rw.GetMol(); Chem.SanitizeMol(mol); mol=Chem.AddHs(mol)
xy=[(212,142),(315,82),(420,142),(420,263),(316,322),(212,263),(524,82),(627,142),(627,263),(524,321),(732,321),(732,443),(627,502),(524,443),(524,202),(627,22),(732,82),(850,82),(110,323),(380,443),(627,622)]
conf=Chem.Conformer(mol.GetNumAtoms())
for ix,(x,y) in enumerate(xy): conf.SetAtomPosition(ix,Point3D(x/100,-y/100,0))
# N and q are on hashed bonds behind the drawing. Alcohol O is on a solid wedge.
for ix,z in [(14,-1),(16,-1),(20,1)]:
    p=conf.GetAtomPosition(ix); p.z=z; conf.SetAtomPosition(ix,p)
# The two shown hydrogens are dashed. Complete the other two stereo H positions.
for ix,(x,y,z) in {7:(627,142,1),8:(727,206,-1),12:(627,502,-1),13:(524,560,-1)}.items():
    hi=[n.GetIdx() for n in mol.GetAtomWithIdx(ix).GetNeighbors() if n.GetSymbol()=='H'][0]
    conf.SetAtomPosition(hi,Point3D(x/100,-y/100,z))
mol.AddConformer(conf)
Chem.AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure(mol,replaceExistingTags=True)
for atom in mol.GetAtoms():
    if atom.GetIdx() not in [7,8,9,12,13]: atom.SetChiralTag(Chem.ChiralType.CHI_UNSPECIFIED)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(mol,cleanIt=True,force=True)
print('Formula',rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula(mol))
print('SMILES',Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.RemoveHs(mol)))
for ix in [7,8,9,12,13]:
    at=mol.GetAtomWithIdx(ix)
    print(names[ix], at.GetChiralTag(), at.GetProp('_CIPCode') if at.HasProp('_CIPCode') else '')
mol.RemoveAllConformers()
params=AllChem.ETKDGv3();params.randomSeed=235; params.numThreads=0
cids=AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(mol,numConfs=64,params=params)
print('Embedded',len(cids))
res=AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(mol,numThreads=0,maxIters=3000)
print('Energy best', min(res,key=lambda x:x[1]))
best=min(range(len(cids)),key=lambda i:res[i][1]); conf=mol.GetConformer(cids[best])
with open('answer.xyz','w') as out:
    out.write(f'{mol.GetNumAtoms()}\n3D structure from mol_0235.png; explicit hydrogens; angstroms\n')
    for at in mol.GetAtoms():
        p=conf.GetAtomPosition(at.GetIdx())
        out.write(f'{at.GetSymbol()} {p.x:.8f} {p.y:.8f} {p.z:.8f}\n')
Chem.MolToMolFile(mol,'answer.mol',confId=cids[best])
# confirm that optimized structure retains all assigned stereochemistry
check=Chem.Mol(mol)
Chem.AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure(check,confId=cids[best],replaceExistingTags=True)
for ix in [7,8,9,12,13]:
    assert check.GetAtomWithIdx(ix).GetChiralTag()==mol.GetAtomWithIdx(ix).GetChiralTag()
print('Validated stereochemistry and saved answer.xyz')
PY
python build.py
